paragraphs.source_en: They do not pursue us past the Rubicon Beacons, where we are joined by our small fleet as well as those of the Cordovan, the Telemanuses, the Norvo. I hope more will flock to our banners after today’s last surprise.

paragraphs.source_en: I examine our wake—naval detritus. Bodies of men and women float behind my vessel. They came out of cracked and punctured ships. Some are still alive but will soon freeze or suffocate. More dead in my path. How many will it take?

units.source_en: I examine our wake—naval detritus.
Bodies of men and women float behind my vessel.
They came out of cracked and punctured ships.
Some are still alive but will soon freeze or suffocate.
More dead in my path.
How many will it take?

paragraphs.source_en: I leave Orion the bridge. Sevro and I find our way to the engineering bay, where we have Oranges cut us out of our mangled suits. We rush from there to the hangar, a vast metal depot scattered with ships, equipment, and now broken men. Yellows dart about aiding the wounded and carting them off to the sickbay, Grays and Oranges helping carry.

paragraphs.source_en: Weed prods several unarmed Golds with his razor. Pebble and Harpy help the Yellows. My eyes search frantically for her. I find her under one of the battered stork’s wings, speaking with her father. A long wound mangles her left arm. I don’t mention it. They were boarded by a leechCraft, and managed to sheave the other off when entering the hangar.

るときにどうにかもう

paragraphs.source_en: “We’ve put the bulk of the Sovereign’s fleet behind us,” I tell Augustus.

units.source_en: “We’ve put the bulk of the Sovereign’s fleet behind us,” I tell Augustus.

paragraphs.source_en: “Where is Quinn?” Sevro asks sharply. “Did they get her to the medBay yet?”

units.source_en: “Where is Quinn?”
Sevro asks sharply.
“Did they get her to the medBay yet?”

paragraphs.source_en: Mustang does not answer. Instead, she looks to the ramp of the stork, where Roque descends, carrying Quinn in his arms. She’s pale. Long. And lifeless. Sevro does not move. Does not speak. His nostrils flare as a breath catches in his chest, a pitiful sob locked tight in the boy who never cries. He goes numb. Ghostlike. And I reach for him, but he pulls away not in anger, but in confusion, as though he was told the future once, and this reality is not what was promised. He stumbles backward, away from her body, looking around, before turning and fleeing the hangar.

paragraphs.source_en: Roque walks past me with Quinn. His face is slack and tired. He wants to say something bitter, but he bites his tongue and just shakes his head at me. He still does not know why I attacked him in his room before the gala. And now this. I’ve never seen him so broken.

ja.t: きたがっているが、こらえて、ただ

paragraphs.source_en: “Look at her,” he tells me. “Darrow, look at your friend.”

units.source_en: “Look at her,” he tells me.
“Darrow, look at your friend.”

paragraphs.source_en: I look at Quinn and feel everything go quiet. Here she is, peaceful in death. Why can we not breathe life back into her? Why can we not simply restart the day? Do everything right. Save the ones we love.

ja.t: すことができないのだろう。

paragraphs.source_en: Roque moves away with Quinn toward the hangar’s transparent pulse field, which opens into space. He’s bent and broken as he walks to the stars to push his lost girl out amongst them.
